newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso recoups lost ground on foreign return.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso recoups lost ground on foreign return.

text.p: The Mexican peso clawed back some lost ground in late trade on Thursday to close firmer as some foreign investors stepped back into the market after a session where speculation prevailed, traders said.
"The peso began to recover after midsession as mutual funds began to step back into Mexico," said a trader.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour counterpart closed 2.5 and four centavos firmer, respectively, at 7.96/7.98 and 7.94/7.96 per dollar.
The 48-hour peso had weakened by seven centavos in early trade to 8.0550/8.0750 per dollar.
The same-day peso had closed earlier two centavos weaker at 8.0000/8.0200 per dollar.

Traders put down early weakness to speculators taking advantage of uncertainty over U.S. presidential and congressional elections and the Mexican government's budget and economic policy criteria for 1997.
Some dealers, they said, forced the peso down in order to sell dollars they had for more pesos and then take profits.
"Foreign traders knew the market was illiquid (in dollar terms), so it was easy for them to force the peso down and take profits," a trader said.
Traders said they thought the peso might return to trade below 7.95 per dollar after the U.S. elections.
